query: Which simple heuristic baselines (low-frequency tag rules, rule-based boundary checks) and ablation studies are necessary to benchmark complex detectors?

response.query: Which simple heuristic baselines (low-frequency tag rules, rule-based boundary checks) and ablation studies are necessary to benchmark complex detectors?
response.answer: Simple heuristic baselines include low-frequency tag rules and rule-based boundary checks. Ablation studies are essential to benchmark complex detectors by removing parts to evaluate their impact. These baselines and studies help establish a performance baseline for more advanced models.

results.title: Accepted Papers - IEEE SaTML 2026
results.content: > Model fingerprint detection techniques have emerged as a promising approach for attributing AI-generated images to their source models, with high detection accuracy in clean settings. We present the first systematic security evaluation of these techniques, formalizing threat models that encompass both white- and black-box access and two attack goals: fingerprint removal, which erases identifying traces to evade attribution, and fingerprint forgery, which seeks to cause misattribution to a target model. We also identify a utility-robustness trade-off: methods with the highest attribution accuracy are often vulnerable to attacks, whereas more robust approaches tend to be less accurate. These findings highlight the urgent need for developing model fingerprinting techniques that are robust in adversarial settings. We address this gap by introducing two new attacks: (i) an adaptation of multivariate LiRA, a state-of-the-art MIA originally developed for classification models, to the time-series forecasting setting, and (ii) a novel end-to-end learning approach called Deep Time Series (DTS) attack.
